status: Mechanistic secondary analysis specified after the cold b=2 quotient result was known. Exploratory validation, not preregistered discovery or new confirmation.
source: Existing checksum-verified L20 endpoint files only, beta indices 0,5,7,8,9. Use quotient.tables/marginals: one seeded cubic frame per parent, all 8000 periodic translations, opposite visible corners and two radially extended exterior sites, b=1,2,3,4,5 empty layers. Each translation has exactly four ordered ternary labels (vacant=0,A=1,B=2). No generated configurations, trajectories, new sampling or test-fold evaluation.
split: Original disjoint 10240 fit and 2048 validation parents from l20_pairs.partition. Use grouped tables of 64 parents. The shuffle exchanges complete exterior rows at common anchors cyclically within batches of 16 validation parents (no fixed points, never crosses uncertainty clusters). Split independence is by parent, not translation or frame.
models: Add Jeffreys pseudocount 1/2 to each of 81 joint cells on training only, then normalize. Starting from uniform, cyclic IPF successively matches every k-way margin for k=1,2,3, stopping only when every maximal margin has max absolute error <=2e-13 (failure above tolerance is fatal). The smoothed empirical law is saturated. All score models normalize the JOINT over Y conditional on the same observed V. Independent-block null is p(V)p(Y), permitting both arbitrary within-pair marginals. Each single-cross-edge fit starts with both within-block edges and adds only the indicated Vi:Yj edge. Scores conditional on V exclude spurious reward for fitting the input marginal. The one-body vs block-null comparison includes the cost of ignoring within-Y dependence and is not interpreted as transmitted information.
quantizer: At each buffer select the exactly optimal 4-label partition on cold index-9 unsmoothed training counts, as in quotient.solutions, then freeze that code across temperatures. For each temperature, aggregate the saturated and pairwise fitted joint by the SAME code before normalizing Y|H. This compares decoder conditionals at fixed H and quantifies whether pairwise joint physics can account for the documented quantized signal; it does not reoptimize the pairwise encoder. The 81-cell prior is common to both, not re-added on the compressed alphabet.
estimands: All validation gaps are mean paired log probability ratios, nats per case, for frozen decoders. Report saturated minus pairwise, triple minus pairwise, saturated minus triple, hierarchy and individual cross edges minus block-null, and loss from the cold K4 compression. Pairwise gain divided by saturated gain is a predictive fraction, not a unique causal attribution or MI decomposition; ratios unbounded when denominator is unresolved. Fit-table MI is a descriptive finite-table number, not a population estimate corrected for bias. Held-out gains against an estimated block-null are NOT guaranteed lower bounds on mutual information.
intervals: Use t intervals over 32 nonoverlapping equal validation clusters of 64 parents. Report paired, shuffled and paired-minus-shuffled means. Additionally, for the unquantized saturated/pairwise/triple contrasts and their block-null gains propagate training reference-fit variability by a 16-way equal delete-group jackknife (640 parents/deletion) of the expected log-ratio on fixed validation counts. Add training and validation variances from independent folds; use conservative min df=15. Jackknife is first-order, not a guarantee against finite-sample training bias. Other intervals condition on trained reference and code. Two-sided nominal 95% and approximate familywise 95% Bonferroni t intervals; denominator budgets all reported score intervals and ratio sets over all 25 panels. Dependence between contrasts/temperatures does not require independence for Bonferroni. Ratio sets use paired Fieller inversion conditional on fitted models and may be unbounded. These intervals do not correct for previous uses of this validation archive.
decision: Prespecified practical tolerance for the full-channel saturated-minus-pairwise gain is +/-1e-5 nats per case (roughly 10% of the previously documented b2 projected cold quantizer signal). Call practical equivalence of these predictive scores only when BOTH the conditional and training-jackknife simultaneous two-sided intervals lie strictly inside that band; a nonsignificant difference is not equivalence. No claim that exact higher-order interactions vanish.
transfer: SVD of the centered whitened unsmoothed empirical TRAIN joint, diag(pV)^(-1/2) [P-pV pY^T] diag(pY)^(-1/2), restricted to positive support. Report all nontrivial singular values, standardized functions, weighted marginal contrast correlations, and basis-invariant squared contrast projection for tied singular subspaces. Vanishing or constant contrasts have no defined loading. Project on each side into weighted additive single-site functions (orthogonal to constant) and their orthogonal connected-pair complement. Report all four squared Frobenius block norms, which partition chi-square, NOT MI or conditional log score. Compare occupancy, species A/B, occupancy parity, A-bit parity, species equality, and sums/differences. In particular, a connected-pair component of normalized transfer need not imply a higher-than-pairwise Gibbs potential.
controls: Nonuniform analytically independent blocks, pure modular ternary triple and quadruple parity laws mixed with uniform noise (all probabilities strictly positive); exact population cross-entropy differences must have the expected hierarchy and spectral allocation. No synthetic lattice or resampling chain. Show beta0 as an archive control and the independent-parent exterior-row shuffle at every temperature; neither is assumed to yield exactly zero on this finite archive.
output: interactions.csv (validation gaps and uncertainty); tables.json (training/validation 81-cell counts, fitted joints, IPF residuals, quantizers, transfer modes and ratios); controls.json (analytical checks); interactions.png (distance profiles for all beta indices, cold paired score gaps and spectral components).
